implementation_notes: The C++ case has two extra wrinkles the C case does not. Templates: an uninstantiated template is not an anchor but an instantiated-and-unused one is, and the compiler only tells you about the latter if nothing odr-uses it. Inline functions and class member functions defined in-class are only emitted when odr-used, so `-Wunused-function` under-reports and the linker is the real instrument. Virtual functions are the sharpest edge: a virtual method is reachable through the vtable by dispatch from anywhere, so `grep` cannot establish that it is dead, and removing one is a silent behaviour change if a derived class or a framework expects it.
idiom_name: unused translation unit, unused inline, unused virtual
pitfalls: A virtual function on a type used with `dynamic_cast` or framework reflection is reachable and removing it is an ABI change.
`using` declarations and template specialisations can keep a symbol alive with no visible reference.
Headers included by nobody still cost parse time in every TU that does include them transitively — anchor cost is paid at compile time even when the code never links.
